title: PerMIT: Securing Persistent Memory for LLM Agents via Machine-Checked Integrity Theorems and Scalable Community Trust
abstract: arXiv:2610.28987v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Persistent memory is a largely undefended surface for injection and poisoning, and the same risk limits memory sharing among agents. We present PerMIT, a memory architecture with provable integrity guarantees under an explicit trust assumption: only user-typed inputs and values confirmed at a gate are trusted. PerMIT mediates the release and use of untrusted environment-derived values through a finite memory interface, while preserving agent-driven multi-turn planning and tool choice. Over this finite interface, we prove two integrity theorems that are also machine-checked in Lean 4, which together ensure that environment-derived memory reaches a sensitive action only if confirmed at the gate and influences the agent's behavior only through what the gate displays. Every attack in our threat model thereby reduces to a single auditable decision, which a human, an LLM verifier, or both can make in practice. On Trojan Hippo, PerMIT records z

translated_title: PerMIT：通过机器校验的完整性定理与可扩展的社区信任保障LLM智能体的持久内存安全
translated_abstract: 持久内存是一个在很大程度上缺乏防御的注入与投毒攻击面，同样的风险也限制了智能体之间的内存共享。我们提出了PerMIT，这是一种在明确信任假设下具有可证明完整性保证的内存架构：只有用户手动键入的输入以及在门控处确认过的值才是可信的。PerMIT通过一个有限的内存接口来调解不可信的环境衍生值的释放与使用，同时保留了智能体驱动的多轮规划与工具选择能力。在这个有限接口之上，我们证明了两个完整性定理，并且这些定理在Lean 4中经过了机器校验，二者共同确保：环境衍生的内存内容只有在门控处获得确认后才能触及敏感操作，并且只能通过门控所显示的内容来影响智能体的行为。因此，威胁模型中的每一次攻击都可归结为单一的、可审计的决策，在实践中可由人类、LLM验证器或二者共同作出。在Trojan Hippo基准上，PerMIT记录了……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: PerMIT提出了一种基于明确信任假设的LLM智能体持久内存安全架构，通过有限的内存接口调解不可信的环境衍生值，并借助两个经Lean 4机器校验的完整性定理，将威胁模型中的所有注入/投毒攻击归结为单一的、可由人类或LLM验证器审计的门控决策，从而提供可证明的完整性保证。
en_tdlr: PerMIT is a persistent memory architecture for LLM agents that provides provable integrity guarantees by mediating untrusted environment-derived values through a finite memory interface, backed by two Lean 4 machine-checked theorems that reduce every injection/poisoning attack to a single auditable gate decision made by a human, an LLM verifier, or both.
